additions.title: Fatty acid-derived dicarboxylic acid modification mitigates human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-targeted antibody–drug conjugate-induced interstitial lung disease
additions.abstract: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) has transformed human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-targeted cancer therapy, but its clinical use is constrained by interstitial lung disease (ILD), a potentially fatal toxicity linked to pulmonary macrophage handling of circulating antibody-drug conjugates. Here, we develop fatty acid-derived dicarboxylic acid modification as a host-facing antibody engineering strategy to reduce alveolar macrophage-associated pulmonary uptake while preserving HER2-directed tumor specificity. Using N-hydroxysuccinimide ester chemistry, we coupled mono-N-hydroxysuccinimide-activated esters of C4, C12, and C18 aliphatic dicarboxylic acids to surface-accessible amino groups on trastuzumab, generating C4-DA-, C12-DA-, and C18-DA-modified conjugates with a retained distal carboxyl group and an average of approximately four added groups per antibody. Dicarboxylic acid modification preserved HER2 binding but reduced Fcγ receptor engagement in a chain-length-dependent manner, with C18-DA modification abolishing detectable FcγRIII binding under the tested conditions. This receptor-level shift reduced macrophage-associated antibody uptake by up to approximately 42% across mouse alveolar macrophages, mouse macrophages, and human macrophage-like cells, while maintaining HER2-positive tumor-cell binding and endocytic trafficking. In vivo, dicarboxylic acid-modified trastuzumab reduced pulmonary deposition without compromising tumor localization. C18-DA-modified trastuzumab showed greater mouse serum albumin binding, and the corresponding antibody-drug conjugate exhibited increased systemic exposure and reduced clearance. In a repeated-dose immunocompetent model, C12-DA- and C18-DA-modified T-DXd reduced lung weight, selected inflammatory cytokine responses, and pneumonia/ILD-like lesion incidence, with C18-DA modification lowering lesion incidence from 100% to 41.7%. Importantly, dicarboxylic acid-modified T-DXd retained HER2-dependent cytotoxicity and antitumor efficacy in HER2-positive models. Together, our study expands antibody-drug conjugate design beyond tumor targeting and payload optimization, showing that engineering host-cell recognition can improve safety while preserving antitumor function.

additions.title: Masitinib-loaded poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) nanoparticles reinstate lysosomal acidification and drive immunomodulation in Alzheimer's disease
additions.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) poses a formidable therapeutic challenge due to its intricate pathological mechanisms and the blood-brain barrier (BBB). Via transcriptomic analyses and experimental validation, we identify that a malignant neuro-immune pathological cycle, driven by neuronal lysosomal acidification dysfunction and microglial immune activation, potently accelerates AD pathogenesis. Then, we engineer a simple bifunctional intranasal delivery system (PLGA@M) by loading masitinib into poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) nanoparticles. Following intranasal administration, PLGA@M bypasses the BBB to enter the brain directly via olfactory and trigeminal nerves. PLGA degrades to release acidic moieties, lowering lysosomal pH and restoring autophagic flux, while masitinib inhibits microglial colony stimulating factor 1 receptor signaling, attenuating microglial proliferation, excessive activation and neuroinflammation. Behavioral assays confirm that PLGA@M markedly reverses cognitive deficits in AD mice. This system upgrades PLGA from a mere carrier to a therapeutic component, featuring simplicity, high efficiency and great clinical translation potential.

additions.title: Membrane retention and cellular uptake of click conjugated cargos
additions.abstract: Metabolic glycan labeling offers a facile yet powerful method to functionalize cell membranes with clickable chemical tags for subsequent conjugation of cargos via bioorthogonal click chemistries. However, the membrane retention and cellular uptake of covalently conjugated cargos, which is distinct from natural systems where cells interact with extracellular cargos via electrostatic or hydrophobic interactions, remain elusive. Here, we developed a dibenzocyclooctyne (DBCO)-functionalized polyacrylic acid (PAA) probe system that enables simultaneous detection of overall cellular uptake and membrane retention, and investigated how the molecular weight, valency, and hydrophobicity of DBCO-PAAs impact their membrane retention and cell uptake rates after click conjugation to azido-labeled cells. PAA with lower molecular weights exhibited enhanced cell-conjugation efficiency and prolonged membrane retention compared to higher molecular-weight counterparts. Increasing DBCO density improved the cell-conjugation efficiency and membrane retention, while altering the hydrophobicity of PAA induced minimal changes in the membrane retention and cellular internalization rates. We further uncovered energy dependent endocytosis and caveolin-dependent pathways as the main endocytic routes for the covalently conjugated cargos. We also studied the membrane retention of DBCO-functionalized phycoerythrin and allophycocyanin, two representative fluorescent proteins, on azido-labeled cells, which exhibited cargo and cell type-dependent membrane retention. Our study comprehensively assesses the membrane retention and cellular uptake of covalently conjugated cargos and could guide future design of cell-targeting clickable agents.

additions.title: Engineering long-circulating deferoxamine targeting the innate immunity of neutrophil ferroptosis for systemic lupus erythematosus treatment
additions.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is characterized by dysregulation of both innate and adaptive immunity, in which ferroptosis-mediated neutrophil death has been implicated in disease progression. However, the clinical application of ferroptosis inhibitors remains limited by rapid systemic clearance and poor pharmacokinetic profiles. Here, we report a full positron emission tomography (PET)-guided strategy for pharmacokinetic engineering of ferroptosis inhibitors through albumin hitchhiking. By incorporating an albumin-binding motif into deferoxamine (DFO), we developed a series of albumin-hitchhiking conjugates and employed in vivo PET imaging-assisted evaluation to identify a long-circulating molecule, termed LACNE. Blood pharmacokinetic analysis showed that LACNE exhibited an estimated terminal blood half-life of 235.94 min, approximately 17-fold longer than that of DFO (13.74 min). Mechanistically, LACNE was preferentially taken up by activated neutrophils via Fcγ receptor-mediated internalization under inflammatory conditions, resulting in effective suppression of neutrophil ferroptosis. Consequently, LACNE reduced autoimmune responses, alleviated renal injury, and improved disease manifestations in lupus-prone mice. Collectively, these findings establish a PET-guided albumin-hitchhiking approach for pharmacokinetic optimization and targeted delivery of ferroptosis inhibitors, providing a promising strategy for precision treatment of SLE.

additions.title: A Hsp70-dependent bioorthogonal platform for tumor-specific drug release
additions.abstract: Here, we present a novel Hsp70-dependent bioorthogonal prodrug platform that integrates tumor-selective accumulation with inverse electron-demand Diels-Alder (IEDDA) chemistry to enable spatiotemporally controlled drug release. We constructed a tetrazine (Tz)-functionalized Hsp70 inhibitor Tz-S1g, along with trans-cyclooctene (TCO)-caged prodrugs TCO-DOX and TCO-MZ1. Tz-S1g selectively accumulates in tumor cells via high-affinity binding to overexpressed and activated Hsp70, which is characteristic of malignant cells. In tumor microenvironments, Tz-S1g rapidly triggers the IEDDA reaction to liberate active DOX and MZ1, and fully restores cytotoxicity, and BRD4 degradation in tumor cells, whereas minimal activation and cytotoxicity occur in normal cells. In vivo studies have shown that this strategy can effectively inhibit tumor growth in both B16 tumor-bearing mice and MDA-MB-231 tumor-bearing mice, while avoiding systemic toxicity. This Hsp70 bioorthogonal strategy offers a general, safe, and efficient platform for the tumor-specific activation of chemotherapeutic agents and PROTACs, significantly improving therapeutic selectivity and safety.

additions.title: An injectable dynamic double-network hydrogel induces synergistic tumor pyroptosis and immune activation for potent anti-cancer immunity
additions.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, largely due to the limited efficacy of conventional systemic therapies. Herein, we report an injectable dynamic double-network hydrogel Gel@R/N, composed of poly(vinyl alcohol) and tannic acid crosslinked via dynamic boronate ester bonds, for the localized co-delivery of an immune adjuvant (R848) and a pyroptosis inducer (Nigericin) to achieve synergistic tumor ablation and immune activation. The self-healing capacity and pH-responsive drug release properties of this hydrogel enables precise intratumoral administration and sustained release within the acidic tumor microenvironment. Mechanistically, nigericin induces mitochondrial dysfunction and reactive oxygen species accumulation, thus activating the NLRP3/caspase-1/GSDMD pathway to trigger pyroptosis with a cell death rate of 26.4% alongside immunogenic cell death. The release of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) caused by pyroptosis, further promoted dendritic cell maturation to 20.8% and macrophage repolarization toward the pro-inflammatory M1 phenotype reaching 23.0%. Concurrently, R848 activates Toll-like receptor signaling to promote dendritic cell maturation and antigen presentation. Additionally, the hydrogel system effectively suppressed tumor growth in both subcutaneous and orthotopic hepatocellular carcinoma models, accompanied by a 1.55-fold increase in intratumoral CD8+ T cells infiltration and a 65.9% reduction in immunosuppressive cell populations. Overall, this work presents a safe and effective hydrogel-based platform for synergistic pyroptosis induction and immune activation, which offers a promising strategy for hepatocellular carcinoma immunity.

additions.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Nanomedicine Development: From Rational Design to Manufacturing Optimization
additions.abstract: The translation of nanomedicines remains constrained by persistent bottlenecks, including complex design parameters, unpredictable in vivo behavior, and low diagnostic accuracy. Artificial intelligence (AI), with its advanced data processing and learning algorithms, offers new solutions to these challenges by learning from heterogeneous data and supporting decision-making throughout nanomedicine development. This review summarizes the AI methods and modeling workflows relevant to nanomedicine and surveys their applications in rational nanomaterial design, prediction of in vivo fate and nano-bio interactions, theranostic imaging analysis, and formulation and manufacturing optimization. This review further discusses the main barriers that currently limit translation, which largely concern data, model reliability, and computational cost. Future progress will depend on better data resources, more generalizable and interpretable models, and closer integration of AI with experimental and mechanistic approaches. We believe that through these advances, AI-enabled nanomedicine will ultimately achieve more reliable and translatable outcomes.

additions.title: Nanoengineering strategies for precision regulation of chimeric antigen receptor T-cell-induced cytokine release syndrome
additions.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy faces a critical clinical hurdle: cytokine release syndrome (CRS). Current CRS management strategies have limited selectivity and may interfere with CAR-T cell antitumor activity, highlighting the need for more targeted and precisely controllable interventions. Nanoengineering offers a promising approach to address these limitations by enabling the spatiotemporally controlled monitoring and modulation of inflammatory responses, with the potential to mitigate excessive cytokine release while preserving CAR-T cell therapeutic efficacy, driving a paradigm shift toward programmable, proactive immune regulation. This review systematically examines nanointervention strategies for mitigating CAR-T-induced CRS, including molecular monitoring, cytokine clearance, targeted delivery, stimulus-responsive systems, biomimetic designs, and genetic reprogramming. These approaches enable precise intervention across multiple stages-from early inflammation detection and localized neutralization to source-level cellular engineering. Finally, we discuss challenges in biosafety, clinical translation, and the potential of artificial intelligence-driven predictive platforms. Nanotechnology offers a transformative pathway to redefine CRS from an unpredictable complication into a manageable therapeutic window, paving the way for safer next-generation cellular immunotherapies.

additions.title: An anti-ferroptosis hydrogel enhances mesenchymal stem cell spheroid-based gene delivery for spinal cord injury repair
additions.abstract: Stem cell-based gene delivery systems represent a promising approach for sustained and localized therapeutic factor delivery after spinal cord injury (SCI). However, their in vivo performance is often limited by poor graft survival in the hostile lesion microenvironment. Here, using glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor (GDNF) as a representative therapeutic cargo, we established a mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) spheroid (MS)-based GDNF gene delivery system (GF-MS). Notably, we identified that ferroptosis served as an important and targetable limiting factor restricting graft persistence and transgene output in SCI rats, as supported by transcriptomic enrichment of ferroptosis-related pathways, mitochondrial damage, ferrous iron accumulation, excessive lipid peroxidation, impaired SLC7A11/GPX4 antioxidant defense, and reduced GDNF expression in implanted GF-MS. To overcome this limitation, we constructed a ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1)-loaded reactive oxygen species (ROS)-scavenging hydrogel (RH-Fer), which can scavenge excessive microenvironmental ROS and responsively release Fer-1. In vivo experiments demonstrated that RH-Fer effectively mitigated ferroptosis and prolonged graft persistence of GF-MS. Consequently, this combined system enhanced local GDNF expression during the therapeutic window and promoted neural tissue repair and functional recovery in SCI rats. These findings highlight ferroptosis-targeted microenvironment modulation as an effective strategy to optimize stem cell-based gene delivery for SCI repair.

additions.title: Dual drug delivery via integrin-targeted nanoparticles enhances therapeutic efficiency in BRAFV600E colon cancer
additions.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) patients possessing the BRAFV600E mutation often fail to respond to current first-line therapies and are associated with poor prognosis, despite the advent of orally delivered small molecule inhibitors (SMIs) targeting the RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK signaling pathway. Thus, further improvements are required at a formulation and delivery level in order to enhance survival of these patients. Here we have formulated nanoparticles (NPs) made from biodegradable PEGylated poly(lactide-co-glycolide) (PEG-PLGA) polymers, co-loaded with the SMIs, encorafenib (a BRAFV600E inhibitor) and trametinib (a MEK1/2 inhibitor) and decorated with the integrin-targeting moiety, cyclic arginine-glycine-aspartate (cRGD), that are capable of significantly enhancing therapeutic effectiveness upon intravenous (IV) delivery in a xenogeneic CRC model when compared to the soluble SMIs delivered IV at equivalent doses. Pharmacokinetic analyses revealed actively targeted NPs could deliver the SMIs more efficiently to the tumor than IV-administered SMIs in soluble form while also reducing their accumulation in the skin, an off-target site often associated with the dose-limiting side-effects of trametinib. This work is the first to demonstrate the therapeutic benefit of targeted nano-based co-delivery of SMIs in BRAFV600E-CRC and warrants further progression toward clinical studies in order to improve CRC patient survival outcomes.

additions.title: Bioorthogonal sticky-PROTACs for targeted and sustained protein degradation
additions.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) can catalytically eliminate disease-driving proteins, but nonspecific exposure, rapid clearance, and concentration-dependent hook effects limit their tumor selectivity and durability. Here, we report a kinetically programmed bioorthogonal sticky PROTAC (VPT) that temporally separates tumor capture from prodrug activation. Tetrazine (Tz) handles were selectively installed on HER2-overexpressing tumor cells through antibody-directed metabolic glycoengineering. VPT integrates a trans-cyclooctene (TCO) group for rapid Tz-mediated covalent anchoring with a vinyl ether (VE) cage for slower Tz-triggered release of an active BRD4 degrader. The TCO-Tz ligation proceeded approximately 4890-fold faster than VE-Tz cleavage, enabling rapid tumor-cell retention followed by sustained local activation. In HER2-pretargeted cells, VPT prolonged BRD4 degradation after washout, showed no evident hook effect within the tested concentration range. Bioorthogonal anchoring also maintained tumor-associated fluorescence for up to 120 h. In SKOV3 and BT474 xenografts, HER2-MTz plus VPT achieved tumor growth inhibition rates of 85.8% and 95.7%, respectively, outperforming the corresponding non-sticky control. This dual-kinetics design provides a generalizable strategy for coupling tumor-selective retention with sustained in situ PROTAC activation.

additions.title: Stimuli-responsive CRISPR-based genome editing delivery system for cancer treatment: A review of fundamentals and applications
additions.abstract: Cancer remains a leading cause of mortality worldwide. Conventional modalities, namely surgery, radiotherapy, chemotherapy, and immunotherapy, continue to face substantial limitations. The advent of gene therapy, particularly CRISPR-based genome editing, offers new opportunities to overcome these barriers. Nuclease systems such as CRISPR/Cas9 enable precise excision of mutant alleles and targeted insertion of exogenous sequences by harnessing endogenous DNA-repair pathways, achieving durable and accurate genomic modification; derivative tools including CRISPRi, base editing, and prime editing enable diverse forms of gene regulation or precise genome modification through transcriptional repression, base conversion, or related editing mechanisms. To enhance the efficiency, specificity, and spatiotemporal control of CRISPR editing in vivo, sophisticated delivery platforms have been engineered to respond to endogenous tumor-microenvironment cues (e.g., pH, redox potential, hypoxia, ATP, enzymes and microRNAs) or exogenous triggers (e.g., light, ultrasound and magnetic fields). Distinct from material-centric classification schemes, this review organizes these stimuli-responsive systems according to their pathological relevance to the tumor microenvironment (TME), establishing a conceptual framework that links specific TME aberrations with corresponding delivery paradigms. These stimuli-responsive systems represent a major innovation and markedly expand the therapeutic potential of genome editing in oncology. In this review, we summarize the mechanistic basis of CRISPR-based editing, delineate design principles and engineering strategies for stimuli-responsive delivery, and highlight recent advances, outstanding challenges, and future directions toward clinical translation. We aim to provide a concise reference to guide the rational design of gene-editing cancer therapeutics.

original_record.title: Kinetically stabilized nanocondensates via guided co-assembly: resolving solubility-potency mismatches and solvent confounding in drug discovery
original_record.abstract: Physicochemical and vehicle-derived artifacts, such as precipitation and solvent-driven perturbations, often decouple nominal dose from the bioavailable aqueous fraction, leading to distorted potency and mechanism assignments in preclinical assays. Here we introduce e-PASS, a computationally guided co-assembly strategy that prioritizes pharmaceutically relevant excipients and generates kinetically stabilized, drug-rich nanocondensates. These nanocondensates act as dynamic reservoirs that sustain free-compound availability during assay-relevant dilution and handling, thereby improving dosing fidelity and maintaining aqueous exposure, as quantified by AUC-based metrics relative to conventional dimethyl sulfoxide dilution. Across chemically diverse kinase and antifibrotic inhibitors, e-PASS suppresses precipitation artifacts, mitigates dimethyl sulfoxide-driven confounding, and yields concentration-response relationships that more faithfully reflect intrinsic compound activity, with mechanism-consistent responses. Improved chemical availability further translates into enhanced systemic exposure and therapeutic efficacy in tumor and liver-fibrosis models. Together, these results establish nanocondensate reservoirs as a general physicochemical lever to overcome precipitation- and vehicle-derived artifacts and expand screenable chemical space for reliable discovery workflows.

original_record.title: Selective ORgan-Targeting lipid nanoparticles deliver SMAD7 mRNA to fibrotic lungs and attenuate pulmonary fibrosis
original_record.abstract: Fibroblast activation and differentiation into myofibroblasts drive excessive extracellular matrix deposition and irreversible scarring in pulmonary fibrosis, such as idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), underscoring the need for therapies that directly target fibroblast activation. Here, we apply engineered lung-targeting Selective ORgan-Targeting (SORT) lipid nanoparticles for intravenous RNA delivery to fibrotic lungs. In a preclinical model of pulmonary fibrosis, engineered SORT LNPs achieved functional mRNA delivery in approximately 20% of CD45-CD31-EpCAM-Thy1.2+ mesenchymal cells in fibrotic lungs. Mechanistic studies further supported a contributory role of the vitronectin (Vtn)/vitronectin receptor (VtnR) axis in 1A7B13 Lung SORT LNP uptake. Therapeutic delivery of SMAD7 mRNA inhibited fibroblast activation in human lung fibroblast cultures and attenuated pulmonary fibrosis in vivo, resulting in an approximately 40% reduction in histological collagen deposition and a significant reduction in lung hydroxyproline content. Together, these findings establish engineered lung-enriched SORT LNPs as a platform for systemic RNA delivery to fibrotic lungs, including disease-relevant mesenchymal populations, and demonstrate their potential for RNA-based anti-fibrotic therapy.

original_record.title: Engineered self-assembly of mucoadhesive Helicobacter pylori vaccines: CD4+ T cell-dependent immunity prevents bacterial colonization
original_record.abstract: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection represents a significant global health burden, being strongly associated with the development of various gastrointestinal pathologies. Immunization emerges as the most promising strategy for population-level prevention. In this study, we described the rational design of a novel multi-antigenic H. pylori vaccine, which was strategically engineered to target key pathogenic mechanisms: gastric acid survival, mucus layer penetration, epithelial cell adhesion, and virulence factor secretion. Through comprehensive immunoinformatic analysis combining secondary structure prediction and molecular docking simulations, we identified and optimized a multi-epitope construct (UHFV) comprising immunodominant regions from four critical antigens: urease B (UreB, U), flagellin A (FlaA, F), adhesin A (HpaA, H), and vacuolating cytotoxin A (VacA, V). This ensemble of epitopes was subsequently displayed on a self-assembling ferritin (Fn) nanoparticle platform to generate the particulate antigen UHFV-Fn. To further enhance mucosal delivery, we engineered a mucoadhesive delivery system using biocompatible hydroxypropyltrimethyl ammonium chloride chitosan (HACC), which significantly improved antigen stability and bioavailability. The resulting UHFV-Fn@HACC vaccine formulation demonstrated robust protective effect, eliciting potent H. pylori-specific CD4 + T cell responses and showing remarkable prophylactic efficacy in vivo. Such a multi-component vaccine design represents a notable advancement in the development of effective H. pylori immunization strategies.

owner_closed_nonpromoted_methods.title: A supramolecular peptide reprograms PD-L1+ tumor-associated macrophages to enhance antitumor immunity in lung adenocarcinoma

original_record.title: A supramolecular peptide reprograms PD-L1+ tumor-associated macrophages to enhance antitumor immunity in lung adenocarcinoma
original_record.abstract: Despite advances in immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), clinical benefit in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains limited, largely due to a highly immunosuppressive tumor immune microenvironment (TIME). Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), particularly the PD-L1-positive subset (PD-L1 + TAMs), are key mediators of this immunosuppression, yet their functional roles and therapeutic targetability in LUAD are not fully defined. Through integrated analysis of multiplex immunohistochemistry from ICI-treated LUAD patients and public single-cell RNA sequencing data, we identified PD-L1 + TAMs as an M2-polarized population enriched in non-responders and associated with CD8 + T-cell exhaustion and poor overall survival. To address this, we engineered MH-PDBP, a supramolecular peptide nanoplatform via aurophilic self-assembly, coated with mannosylated human serum albumin for selective TAM targeting. Mechanistically, MH-PDBP was preferentially internalized by M2-like macrophages through clathrin-dependent endocytosis, promoting lysosomal degradation of PD-L1, thereby reprogramming macrophages toward an M1 phenotype and enhancing their phagocytic activity. In an orthotopic LUAD mouse model, MH-PDBP monotherapy significantly reduced tumor burden, decreased intratumoral PD-L1 + TAMs, and increased cytotoxic T-lymphocyte infiltration, thereby reinvigorating systemic antitumor immunity. When combined with radiotherapy, MH-PDBP further improved local tumor control, suppressed tumor growth, and remodeled the TIME toward a proinflammatory state without incurring additional systemic toxicity. These findings establish PD-L1 + TAMs as a druggable mediator of immunosuppression in LUAD and propose supramolecular peptide-mediated macrophage reprogramming as a translatable strategy for enhancing antitumor immunity and guiding the rational design of combination therapies.

owner_closed_nonpromoted_methods.title: Macrophage membrane-biomimetic DNA nanocages deliver taurine to reprogram trained immunity for periodontitis therapy

original_record.title: Macrophage membrane-biomimetic DNA nanocages deliver taurine to reprogram trained immunity for periodontitis therapy
original_record.abstract: As one of the most burdensome oral diseases, periodontitis frequently leads to tooth loss and heightens the risk of systemic diseases. A major clinical challenge is that current strategies often fail to resolve chronic inflammation and bone resorption characteristic of its refractory state. Recent research implicates maladaptive trained immunity (TRIM) as a core mechanism, which promotes myeloid cell skewing and amplifies inflammatory responses and bone loss. Single-cell sequencing of peripheral blood mononuclear cells from periodontitis patients identified an elevated inflammatory stress state. Taurine, a sulfur-containing amino acid with known anti-inflammatory properties, offers therapeutic potential, but its application is limited by low oral bioavailability and a lack of target specificity. To address these challenges, a novel therapeutic strategy based on precisely engineered DNA nanocages carrying taurine has been developed. These nanocages are camouflaged with hybrid cell membranes harvested from M2-polarized and trained-immunosuppressive macrophages for targeted monocytes. This biomimetic system is designed to therapeutically correct the dysregulated TRIM state in monocytes and macrophages, effectively inhibiting inflammation and bone destruction. Concurrently, it restores the osteogenic differentiation and mitochondrial function of periodontal ligament cells via immune modulation, establishing a novel strategy for the precise immunotherapy of chronic periodontitis.

owner_closed_nonpromoted_methods.title: M2 macrophage-derived exosomes deliver NGF-modified mRNA to promote comprehensive corneal repair

original_record.title: M2 macrophage-derived exosomes deliver NGF-modified mRNA to promote comprehensive corneal repair
original_record.abstract: The cornea is a unique tissue vital for vision but susceptible to various injuries. Given this complexity, effective regeneration following severe damage requires the coordinated restoration of multiple tissue components, underscoring the need for innovative therapeutic strategies. mRNA technology has emerged as a transformative platform for protein delivery and therapeutic intervention. Chemically modified mRNA (modRNA), with its enhanced stability and reduced immunogenicity, enables transient yet highly efficient protein expression, positioning it as a powerful tool for therapeutic applications. Successful mRNA delivery requires optimized vectors, among which exosomes represent ideal carriers due to their natural anti-inflammatory and reparative properties, high loading capacity, and intrinsic targeting ability. Here, we harnessed M2 macrophage-derived exosomes (M2-Exos) to deliver NGF modRNA (modNGF) for multidimensional corneal repair. This combined delivery system demonstrated robust protein expression, simultaneously promoting tissue regeneration while suppressing inflammation and neovascularization in alkali-burned corneas. Single-cell RNA sequencing further revealed that the system effectively restores injury-induced cellular heterogeneity, promotes epithelial regeneration, reprograms immune cells, and enhances corneal nerve regeneration through neuroglial cell proliferation and modulation. Our findings underscore the synergistic therapeutic effects of M2-Exos and modNGF, establishing this innovative delivery platform as a promising strategy for ocular surface diseases and broader regenerative medicine applications.

owner_closed_nonpromoted_methods.title: Selective silencing of placental anti-angiogenic factors in invasive trophoblasts via membrane-fusion divalent siRNA delivery for preeclampsia therapy

original_record.title: Selective silencing of placental anti-angiogenic factors in invasive trophoblasts via membrane-fusion divalent siRNA delivery for preeclampsia therapy
original_record.abstract: Preeclampsia is a common and severe hypertensive disorder of pregnancy driven by placental dysfunction. In the absence of effective therapies, termination of pregnancy remains the only definitive treatment, resulting in significant maternal and fetal mortality. In this study, single-cell transcriptomic analysis of human placentae identified extravillous trophoblasts as a key pathogenic invasive cell subtype in preeclampsia, characterized by aberrant overexpression of fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 (Flt-1) and endoglin (Eng), the molecular sources of the soluble anti-angiogenic factors sFlt-1 and sEng. To coordinately modulate these pathogenic mediators, this study designed a novel dual-target divalent siRNA (dual-siRNA) to enhance molecular stability and enable simultaneous gene silencing, and further developed a ligand-functionalized membrane-fusogenic liposomal delivery system (iMFlip) targeting receptors highly expressed in invasive trophoblasts for selective dual-siRNA delivery. The optimized iMFlip@dual-siRNA exhibited favorable stability and low protein adsorption properties, and achieved efficient cytosolic siRNA delivery predominantly through membrane fusion, thereby substantially bypassing lysosomal degradation. In vitro, iMFlip@dual-siRNA markedly restored the invasion, migration and angiogenesis of hypoxia-injured HTR-8/SVneo cells. The subsequent pharmacodynamic studies showed that iMFlip@dual-siRNA simultaneously reduced circulating maternal sFlt-1 and sEng levels, alleviated placental vascular dysfunction and inflammatory microenvironment remodeling through reactivation of the PI3K/Akt/eNOS signaling pathway, and consequently improved maternal hypertension, proteinuria, and fetal growth restriction in a preeclamptic mouse model. Collectively, this study established a mechanism-driven therapeutic paradigm that integrated single-cell transcriptomic analysis-guided pathogenic target identification with advanced nucleic acid delivery strategies, offering a promising precision intervention approach for preeclampsia.

owner_closed_nonpromoted_methods.title: Spatially restricted antigen expression by an ionizable lipid nanoparticle enhances mRNA vaccine immunity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa

original_record.title: Spatially restricted antigen expression by an ionizable lipid nanoparticle enhances mRNA vaccine immunity against Pseudomonas aeruginosa
original_record.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a major cause of hospital-acquired infections, yet no licensed vaccine is available. Although mRNA-LNP vaccines offer a flexible platform for antibacterial immunization, conventional formulations are primarily optimized for gene expression and often result in systemic antigen distribution. Here, we developed a novel ionizable lipid, LC3, that enables spatially confined antigen expression following intramuscular administration while enhancing immunostimulatory activity. Compared with SM102-based LNPs, mRNA-LNP LC3 achieved preferential antigen expression at the injection site and draining lymph nodes, with reduced hepatic expression. Mechanistic studies revealed a pronounced decoupling between cellular uptake and productive gene expression, where LC3-based LNPs showed comparable uptake but cell-context-dependent expression differences between hepatocytes and muscle cells, indicating that intracellular processing rather than uptake efficiency governs functional expression and underlies the liver-sparing profile. Single-cell RNA sequencing demonstrated that LNP LC3 vaccination induced a coordinated early immune activation program. Functionally, LNP LC3 elicited stronger humoral and cellular immune responses than LNP SM102 and conferred improved protection against P. aeruginosa, while maintaining a favorable safety profile. Collectively, these results demonstrate that LC3 enables spatially restricted antigen expression through cell-context-dependent intracellular processing, linking localized expression to enhanced immunostimulatory activity. LC3-based LNPs therefore integrate spatial control of antigen expression with improved immune activation, providing a rational strategy for mRNA-LNP vaccine design.
